Then and Now - Greenock's cinema The Ranch remembered

21 hrs ago
Then and Now
History
Nostalgia
Greenock
By Toby Doherty Reporter

Share

0 comments
0:00 / 0:00

THIS week's peek into Inverclyde's pictorial past takes us to a location on Greenock’s high street once home to cowboy standoffs and secret agent espionage.

The Central Picture House, fondly known as The Ranch, stood at 128 West Blackhall Street near Jamaica Street and earned its nickname for its steady stream of Western films.

A coal fire in the foyer offered warmth to moviegoers and was one of the cinema’s most unique features.

The Central first opened its doors at Christmas in 1916, screening silent films including The Victim and Father Three and others. Ticket prices were 4d, 7d, 11d and 1/2d.

Though later converted for sound films, the cinema closed in April 1958.

  • Practical Magic 2 screening soon at Greenock's Waterfront Cinema

  • Fallen Angels comedy starring Rose Byrne to be screened twice in Greenock next month

Despite its nickname, no cowboys featured in its final screenings, which were the British crime thriller The Counterfeit Plan and the American espionage drama Secret File.

The following Monday, the Greenock Telegraph published a nostalgic article, which read: "So 'The Ranch' has closed – the place to which thousands of us used to hurry every Saturday doing the best imitation of a galloping horse that we knew, slapping the seat of our trousers every 10 yards to get there faster.

"Along West Blackhall Street we rode, and even if it was raining we still imagined a cloud of dust behind us."

The Central Picture House. (Image: Newsquest)

The area today. (Image: George Munro)

The closure reflected a wider trend across the country as audiences turned away from the cinema to television.

Our now photo shows the area where the Ranch once stood, now populated by Copperbox, Pepe’s Piri Piri and Dill flowers.

The intervening years since the demolition of the cinema has replaced gallops to the movies with cars parked on the controversial cycle lane.

The new building, while having some interesting design elements of its own, has not recaptured the charm of the Ranch’s architecture.
